newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies surge higher on lighter kills.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies surge higher on lighter kills.

text.p: Packer indications they are continuing to scale back slaughter rates boosted CME pork belly futures for as much as a limit gain and prices stood sharply higher at midsession, traders said. But the same news weighed on hog futures, sources said.

At 1117 CDT, pork belly futures were up 2.875 to 1.450 cents per lb with July up 2.475 after reaching 92.000 cents. Hog futures were down 0.425 to up 0.150 cent with only August up and June off most at 83.050 cents.
Packers' slaughter cutbacks will tighten fresh belly offerings which sparked demand in belly futures, they said.
Commercial short covering and mixed technical buying lifted belly futures into buy stops. Traders also cited unwinding of long hog/short pork belly spreads.
Some traders also noted early indications on next week's Cold Storage report which generally pointed to a bullish number compared to previous years.
Cargill Investor Services, R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock, LFG and Hammer Trading bought. E.D.&F. Man, Refco and locals sold early, pit sources said.

Hog futures were also influenced by statements by IBP Inc and other pork processors that they are curbing slaughter operations due to tight supplies of hogs and pinched margins. Cash hog prices were seen lower again Friday after being quoted mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower Thursday. Futures also looked technically weak after the recent setback in values with fund selling cited on the setback, traders said.
However, losses were limited by strength in pork bellies and the narrowing of the premium of futures to the CME lean hog index, they added.
The latest CME lean hog index rose $1.33 to $82.50 per cwt.
Rosenthal Collins bought July and August while selling June. Prudential Securities and Refco also sold. Rand Financials bought June while being a net seller of July, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought August 76 puts, Rand Financials sold June 81 puts and Rosenthal Collins bought June 82 puts, pit sources added.
